page_title: What’s the Second Job of a Startup CEO?

summary.title: What's the Second Job of a Startup CEO?
summary.one_liner: A startup CEO's second job (Phase 2, scaling the company) is to delegate product work and focus on hiring the leadership team, setting Mission-to-Metrics alignment, and nurturing culture.
keywords: founder transition from doer to manager
when to stop coding as ceo
takeaways: A CEO's job changes across phases: build a product users love, then build a company to capture demand, then invest core profits in new products.
In Phase 2, the CEO must delegate what they did in Phase 1 and focus on three non-delegable tasks: hiring the leadership team, creating purpose and alignment, and nurturing culture.
Define Mission, Strategy, and Metrics in writing, and pick key internal metrics that drive top-line results rather than the top-line results themselves.
Expect at least 25% of senior hires to not work out and act quickly on under-performers.
A sign of success is having substantial unscheduled time to think, because the leadership team runs day-to-day operations.
summary.summary: This Y Combinator Continuity blog essay (archived copy) describes the phases a startup goes through as it scales and what the CEO's job becomes in Phase 2, roughly 20-25 to 400-500 employees. It argues the CEO must stop doing Phase 1 Doer work and focus on three tasks: hiring and coaching a senior leadership team, defining Mission, Strategy and Metrics to create alignment, and shaping culture together with the whole company. It uses examples from Facebook, Stripe, Twitter, SpaceX, Weebly and Pixar's Toy Story 2 to illustrate each point. The piece ends by suggesting that substantial unscheduled thinking time is a clear sign of Phase 2 success.
